- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33) in recent days, model tends to underestimate prices; increase forecast slightly.
- Model consistently overestimates prices in the first 5–7 days of the 30d horizon, especially after recent spikes; apply downward bias to early forecast points.
- After a price spike (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in the next 3–5 days; apply a “cool-down” correction by reducing forecast by 1–2% relative to peak.
- Model shows persistent mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is above 70, true outcome often pulls back; adjust forecast toward historical mean of last 10–15 days if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., +0.67, -0.33, +0.67), model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction.
